F2.Q1: WHAT IS THIS FLOOR MADE OF?**
F2.Q1_WHY: ** The whole surface is one continuous polygonal crack network with no straight joints, no repeating rectilinear module, and no mortar. Cells are irregular five- and six-sided plates, 20–50px across, meeting at Y-junctions — that is shrinkage cracking, not masonry. Base colour sampled at (400,250) is `181,130,83`, a mid-brown; the crack lines sit at `143,103,66` and are hue-shifted toward olive, not simply darker. There are no cut edges anywhere on the floor. The only rectilinear marks are a handful of small stamped rectangle outlines drawn in the crack colour — one at x≈540–560, y≈275–295, another at x≈320–340, y≈343–362 — and they sit *on top of* the organic crack net rather than under it, so they read as a different material's leftovers rather than as the floor's structure. They contradict the answer rather than support it.
